Wiencke, J., Lavelaine, H., Panteix, P.-J., Petitjean, C. and Rapin, C. (2018). Electrolysis of iron in a molten oxide electrolyte. Journal of Applied Electrochemistry 48(1), 115-126. https://doi.org/10.1007/s10800-017-1143-5

Locators are printed journal pages (115-126; PDF page = printed - 114). Laboratory proof-of-concept (ArcelorMittal / Univ. Lorraine) of molten oxide electrolysis of iron at 1823 K in a SiO2-Al2O3-MgO melt with 15 wt% iron oxide, Pt anode, 3 V, 6 h. Loaded (main): description, state of development (r-and-d), operating temperature 1823 K, zero direct process CO2 (qualitative). Other-values: cell voltage, decomposition voltage 0.91 V, cathodic efficiency 36%, anodic efficiency 74-78%, electronic current 11%, and a DERIVED cell-only electricity of ~10,160 kWh/t Fe (uses Faraday constant and Fe molar mass; excludes external furnace heat). The paper prints NO energy per t Fe and no cost; the derived value is lab-cell only and should not be used as a technology SEC (allanore_2015_001 gives the 3,700 kWh/t practical estimate). Not loaded: electrolyte composition/thermodynamics (Tables 1-2, 6), oxygen-ppm time series (figures).
